title: Five representative rehabilitation exercises for MediaPipe joint-angle tracking
scope_note: These are five widely used examples, NOT an evidence-based ranking of the five most common exercises worldwide.
safety_note: Healthy normative ROM is NOT a rehabilitation prescription, required performance threshold, or safe movement limit. A licensed physiotherapist or physician must set diagnosis-, procedure-, and phase-specific limits and goals for each patient. Stop and seek clinical advice for new or escalating symptoms. The software is intended to assist rather than replace clinical assessment.
measurement_note: MediaPipe estimates external landmarks; the resulting angles are approximations, not clinically validated goniometry or intra-articular joint motion. Calibrate cameras, align with the relevant motion plane, track 3D / multi-view consistency where feasible, and validate degree error against a clinical reference before clinical deployment.

exercises.name: Supine heel slide
exercises.purpose: Restore or monitor knee bending range of motion
exercises.setup: Lie supine on a firm surface with both legs initially comfortably extended.
ideal_form: Keep pelvis and trunk reasonably still.
Slide the target heel toward the buttocks along the support surface.
Allow the knee to bend smoothly without rotating the hip markedly or lifting the heel.
Return the heel smoothly to the starting position.
Use only the motion permitted by the treating clinician; do not push through sharp pain.

reference_rom_deg.interpretation: 0° is a straight knee; 135° is an approximate conventional full-flexion reference for healthy adults, not a prescribed post-injury/postoperative target.

illustrative_motion_deg.label: anatomical reference endpoints only; patient may have a much smaller permitted range

flexion_reference_deg.basis: Approximate conventional adult anatomical reference, not a rehabilitation target

measurement.calculation: Knee flexion = 180 - included angle at knee formed by hip-knee-ankle landmarks; 0° denotes full extension (straight leg).
measurement.preferred_camera_view: True lateral (side) view, with the target leg visible, camera fixed; two calibrated cameras can improve 3D assessment.

exercises.name: Seated knee extension (long-arc quadriceps)
exercises.purpose: Monitor active knee straightening while strengthening the quadriceps
exercises.setup: Sit upright on a stable chair with the thighs supported and the target lower leg hanging comfortably.
ideal_form: Keep thigh on the seat and trunk upright.
Straighten the target knee slowly as far as comfortable and permitted.
Avoid swinging, trunk leaning, or lifting the whole thigh.
Pause briefly if prescribed, then lower under control.

reference_rom_deg.interpretation: Full extension corresponds to approximately 0° knee flexion; exercise often starts near 90° knee flexion. Hyperextension varies by person and should not be required automatically.

illustrative_motion_deg.label: common seated movement illustration, not mandatory individual target

flexion_reference_deg.basis: Approximate conventional adult anatomical reference, not a rehabilitation target

measurement.calculation: Knee flexion = 180 - included angle at knee formed by hip-knee-ankle landmarks; 0° denotes full extension (straight leg).
measurement.preferred_camera_view: True lateral (side) view, with the target leg visible, camera fixed; two calibrated cameras can improve 3D assessment.

exercises.name: Standing shoulder forward raise (active flexion)
exercises.purpose: Monitor forward elevation of the arm and shoulder mobility
exercises.setup: Stand or sit tall with arms at sides; use the affected arm only if cleared for active motion.
ideal_form: Raise the arm slowly forward and upward in the sagittal plane.
Keep the trunk upright and avoid leaning backward to increase apparent arm height.
Avoid excessive shoulder shrugging; keep the elbow comfortably straight if permitted.
Lower smoothly to starting position.
If active movement is restricted, therapist may prescribe an assisted version instead.

reference_rom_deg.interpretation: 0–180° is a conventional shoulder-complex reference, not pure glenohumeral motion and not a default rehabilitation goal.

measurement.calculation: In the sagittal plane, angle between vector shoulder->hip (arm-down reference) and shoulder->elbow. 0° = arm at side; ~90° = arm in front; ~180° = arm overhead. Control for trunk lean and scapular motion.
measurement.preferred_camera_view: Lateral (side) view of the target arm, entire shoulder and hip visible.

exercises.name: Seated or standing elbow flexion
exercises.purpose: Restore or monitor elbow bending range of motion
exercises.setup: Sit or stand with upper arm close to the torso, forearm unsupported or supported as prescribed.
ideal_form: Keep the upper arm relatively still at the side.
Bend the elbow slowly, bringing hand toward shoulder.
Avoid swinging the shoulder or leaning the trunk to compensate.
Straighten the elbow under control without forcing end range.

reference_rom_deg.interpretation: 0° indicates full elbow extension; 150° is a conventional healthy elbow flexion reference and may not be appropriate for a particular patient.

measurement.calculation: Elbow flexion = 180 - included angle at elbow formed by shoulder-elbow-wrist. 0° represents straight elbow.
measurement.preferred_camera_view: Side view perpendicular to the forearm movement plane; shoulder, elbow, wrist fully visible.

exercises.name: Standing hip abduction (side leg raise)
exercises.purpose: Monitor hip abduction control and strengthen lateral hip muscles
exercises.setup: Stand upright beside a sturdy support; hold it for balance and keep the stance leg stable.
ideal_form: Keep pelvis approximately level and toes facing forward.
Move the target leg to the side in a slow controlled movement without swinging.
Maintain an upright trunk, avoiding lateral lean, pelvic hike, or twisting.
Return to starting position in a controlled manner.

reference_rom_deg.interpretation: 0–45° is an approximate conventional healthy anatomical range, not a required exercise elevation and may be restricted after surgery.

illustrative_motion_deg.label: anatomical reference endpoints only; standing strengthening exercise may use substantially less

measurement.calculation: Estimate angle of target thigh (hip->knee) away from its neutral downward direction in frontal plane; adjust for pelvic tilt using both hips. A simple trunk-thigh proxy is not isolated clinical hip-joint ROM.
measurement.preferred_camera_view: Frontal view centered on pelvis, both hips and both knees visible; additional calibrated view for rotation and depth.
